messages.author: d560d9e01924933c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] I am using a survey data from a 2-stage sample, is it not necessary to apply population weights using INLA?
parts:
Hi Chigozie,

Just to make sure we are talking about the same thing, survey-weights
are weights used on complex sampling which somehow try to correct
biases on the sampling. For example, you may sample the same number of
people in two different cities, but one city is a way bigger than the
other. So you change the "importance" of the participants from
different cities by giving weights that are proportional to the
population of the city they come from.

So you could use the weights parameters in the INLA function, but you
should do it with extra careful. First thing you should do is to
normalize your sampling weights such as they add up to the sample size
and not as the population size as it is usual in complex sampling. In
complex sampling is it used to leave the weights as they are and
correct the variance estimators after, we don't do that in Bayesian
inference, and this is why you should normalize your sampling weights.

When you include the sampling weights in the weights parameter in
INLA you are actually changing the likelihood to a pseudo-likelihood
instead, and therefore you are no longer doing inference on the
posterior distribution but on the pseudo-posterior distribution of the
parameters. If that is OK for you go ahead. The second issue you
should worry is to make sure you have proper priors, otherwise it is
not guaranteed the your pseudo-posterior is proper.

Another approach, using INLA, was proposed by Vandendijck et al (2016)
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2211675316300690

Cheers,
